card.name: The after twice in antiepileptic risk statements
card.fires_on: The word "the" right after "approximately twice" in the antiepileptic drug pooled-analysis sentence about patients having twice the risk. It also fires weakly on "had" in a group-comparison sentence.

modes.label: Twice the risk
modes.description: The word "the" after "approximately twice" in the pooled analysis of 11 antiepileptic drugs.
modes.example: (mono- and adjunctive therapy) of 11 different AEDs showed that patients randomized to one of the AEDs had approximately twice<< the>> risk (adjusted Relative Risk 1.

modes.label: Group comparison verb
modes.description: The verb "had" after a trial group name, before a higher rate than placebo.
modes.example: adult patients with plaque psoriasis, the TALTZ group<< had>> a higher rate of infections than the placebo

card.plain: It lights up on a repeated stock sentence saying patients on antiepileptic drugs had about twice the risk.
